messages.content: Write a polished 400-to-500-word contemporary American English scene between two adult friends spending an ordinary evening at home after separate long days. Let the scene progress from casual conversation to a quieter topic and then back to something ordinary. Use selective sensory detail, comfortable pauses, and small gestures. Keep emotions understated and avoid a sentimental ending.

The television was on low enough that neither of them had to talk over it.

Casey sat on the floor with a pile of clean clothes beside her.

Morgan came back from the kitchen carrying two glasses.

“Water.”

“Thanks.”

Morgan set hers on the coffee table and dropped onto the couch.

“You've been folding that shirt for five minutes.”

Casey looked down.

“It has a complicated shape.”

“It is a T-shirt.”

“Exactly.”

Morgan laughed.

Casey finished folding it and added it to the stack.

“What are you watching?”

“I don't know.”

“You're the one who turned it on.”

“I know.”

Morgan picked up the remote.

“Do you want something else?”

“Not really.”

“Okay.”

She put the remote down.

A few minutes passed.

Casey sorted the laundry into another pile.

“You ever get tired of doing the same thing?” she asked.

Morgan looked over.

“Laundry?”

“Everything.”

Morgan considered that.

“Sometimes.”

“Yeah.”

“What brought that on?”

Casey shrugged.

“I don't know.”

“You don't have to know.”

Casey smiled faintly.

“You always say that.”

“Because you always think you need a better answer.”

Casey looked at the folded clothes.

“Maybe I do.”

“Maybe.”

The washing machine clicked in the next room.

Morgan leaned forward and picked up one of the shirts.

“This one yours?”

“Yeah.”

“It has paint on it.”

“I know.”

“You keeping it?”

“Probably.”

“Why?”

Casey looked at the faded blue mark near the sleeve.

“Bad painting project.”

“When?”

“A few years ago.”

Morgan nodded.

“Good shirt?”

“Terrible shirt.”

“So why keep it?”

Casey smiled.

“It's comfortable.”

“Fair.”

Morgan tossed it back onto the pile.

Casey finished the laundry and stood.

“What now?” Morgan asked.

“Tea.”

“Good.”

Casey headed toward the kitchen.

“Want anything?”

“No.”

A beat.

“Actually, popcorn.”

Casey looked back.

“You said no.”

“I changed my mind.”

“Fine.”

Morgan smiled.

“That's why you're useful.”

Casey shook her head and disappeared into the kitchen.

The television kept playing.

Morgan reached for the blanket and pulled it over her legs while she waited.
